## Purpose

This SOP defines the protocols for extraction verification, instrument
parameters, operation, and safety requirements for analyzing trace
pesticide residues using Gas Chromatography (GC) coupled with specialized
detectors (e.g., ECD, MS).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Targeted pesticide residue analysis in environmental
  water, soil extracts, and plant tissue digests using GC-ECD or GC-MS.
- **Does not apply to:** LC-amenable pesticides, non-targeted screening,
  or preparative-scale separations.
- **Location:** Environmental analysis laboratories.


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report deviations          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical toxicity:** Pesticide standards, target analytes, and
  extraction solvents (e.g., hexane, dichloromethane, acetone) are highly
  toxic, carcinogenic, or neurotoxic. Inhalation of vapors or skin
  absorption poses a severe chronic health risk.
- **Thermal:** The GC injection port (200--250 °C) and internal column
  oven (50--320 °C) operate at extreme temperatures capable of causing
  instant, severe thermal burns.
- **High-pressure gas cylinders:** Carrier gas cylinders (helium,
  nitrogen, hydrogen) pose mechanical risks if dropped or if regulators
  fail. Hydrogen carrier gas also presents an explosion risk if allowed
  to leak into the oven chamber.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses or chemical splash goggles
- [ ] Laboratory coat (fully fastened)
- [ ] Nitrile or specialized solvent-resistant gloves (e.g., Viton or
      Silver Shield if handling bulk chlorinated solvents)

### Emergency Procedures

In case of chemical spill, gas leak, or equipment failure, refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) or call
campus safety. For compressed gas emergencies, evacuate the area and
contact EH&S.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                         | Notes                                       |
|:-----------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Gas chromatograph            | With autosampler, split/splitless capillary inlet, and detector (ECD or MS) |
| Fused-silica capillary column | e.g., 30 m x 0.25 mm ID, 0.25 µm film thickness, optimized for semi-volatiles |
| Carrier gas cylinders        | Helium or nitrogen (carrier); nitrogen (detector makeup) |
| Inline gas traps             | Moisture, oxygen, and hydrocarbon traps      |

### Consumables

| Item                            | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| GC vials (2 mL amber glass)    | With PTFE-lined septa                    |
| Replacement injection port liners | Deactivated split/splitless with quartz wool plug |
| Low-bleed septa                 | Replace daily or every 50--100 injections |
| Certified pesticide reference standards | Spanning expected concentration range |
| Extraction solvents             | Hexane, dichloromethane, acetone (GC grade) |


## Procedure

### Gas Cylinder and Inlet Verification

1. Verify that gas supply cylinders have sufficient pressure (> 500 psi).
2. Confirm the delivery pressure on the secondary regulator is set to
   manufacturer specifications (typically 60--80 psi).
3. Check the moisture, oxygen, and hydrocarbon traps inline with the gas
   lines. Replace if indicator dyes signal saturation.

### Injection Port Maintenance (Pre-Run Check)

::: {.callout-important}
### Hot Inlet
Ensure the inlet temperature has dropped below 50 °C before opening the
inlet assembly.
:::

1. Replace the injection port septum daily or every 50--100 injections to
   prevent coring fragments from dropping into the liner, which can cause
   sample degradation or carrier gas leaks.
2. Inspect the glass inlet liner. If visible charring, particulate matter,
   or matrix deposits are apparent, replace the liner with a clean,
   deactivated split/splitless liner containing a deactivated quartz wool
   plug.

### Sequence Setup and Sample Loading

1. Prepare standard calibration curves from certified pesticide reference
   materials spanning expected concentration intervals (e.g., 10 µg/L to
   1000 µg/L).
2. Aliquot target sample extracts into clean 2 mL amber glass GC
   autosampler vials to minimize photodegradation of light-sensitive
   pesticides. Cap tightly with PTFE-faced septa crimp or screw tops.
3. Program the injection sequence in the data system software.
   Incorporate the following structural sequence controls:
   - Solvent blanks (hexane/acetone matrix check)
   - Multi-point calibration curves
   - Mid-run continuing calibration verification (CCV) standards every
     10 injections
   - Duplicate sample matrices

### Initiating the GC Run

1. Load the targeted analytical method on the workstation software.
   Verify parameters:
   - **Inlet:** Splitless mode for trace analysis; temperature 250 °C.
   - **Oven temperature program:** Initial 50 °C (hold 1 min), ramp
     10 °C/min to 300 °C (hold 5 min).
   - **Carrier gas flow:** Constant flow mode at 1.2 mL/min helium.
2. Allow all zones (inlet, oven, detector) to reach setpoint equilibrium.
   The software status bar must toggle to a solid `Ready` state.
3. Initiate the programmed sequence. Monitor the initial automated
   injection cycle to ensure the autosampler syringe articulates cleanly
   without bending the needle assembly.
   
### Post-Analysis and Standby Shutdown

1. Review chromatogram baselines for peak symmetry, column bleed spikes,
   or retention time shifting.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Retention Time Drift
If retention times shift significantly, trimming 10--20 cm off the front
edge of the analytical column can restore performance. Document the trim
in the instrument logbook.
:::

2. Upon sequence completion, load a dedicated `Standby` method. This
   method drops the oven temperature below 50 °C and lowers
   inlet/detector temperatures to prolong column life, while maintaining
   a reduced carrier gas purge flow to prevent column phase oxidation.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Initial calibration must meet a correlation coefficient of
  $r^2 \geq 0.995$ across the calibration range.
- CCV standards (run every 10 injections) must recover within ±15% of
  the true value; if recovery falls outside this window, halt the
  sequence and re-calibrate.
- Method blanks must be free of target analyte peaks above the method
  detection limit.
- Duplicate RPD should not exceed 20%.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                 | Container                  | Disposal Method          |
|:---------------------------|:---------------------------|:-------------------------|
| Spent solvents and rinses  | Halogenated or non-halogenated waste jug (as appropriate) | EH&S pickup |
| Used septa, liners, vials  | Solid chemical waste       | Standard hazardous waste |
| Expired pesticide standards | Hazardous waste container  | EH&S pickup              |


## Maintenance

- **Daily:** Replace septum if injection count exceeds 50--100. Inspect
  liner for charring or buildup.
- **Weekly:** Check gas trap indicators; verify carrier gas supply
  pressure.
- **As needed:** Trim or replace the analytical column if baseline
  degradation or retention time shifts persist after liner replacement.
- **Annually:** Full instrument preventive maintenance per manufacturer
  schedule.

## Training Record

Training is documented in the lab training log. Before working
independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Observe a trained operator perform the procedure
3. Perform the procedure under supervision
4. Be signed off by the PI or designated trainer
